purpose: Diagnose the Windows host -> Bluetooth adapter -> CMF Watch Pro 2 path, read-only.

safety.rationale: Every command reads state. No firmware, no pairing change, no driver change, no Bluetooth reset, no write to the watch. Tasks 6 and 7 are passive BLE discovery only: no connection, no GATT reads or writes.
not_included_on_purpose: connect() / GATT service or characteristic reads or writes
netsh winsock reset or any Bluetooth radio reset
firmware flashing, factory reset, NAND writes

setup: Power on the CMF Watch Pro 2 and leave it awake nearby.
Run on the real Windows laptop, in a normal (non-admin) PowerShell window.

how_to_return_evidence.rule: Send raw output. Do not summarise. If a command errors, the error is the finding.

tasks.title: Which machine is this, exactly
tasks.reason: Confirms we are on the real Windows laptop and not some other host. Everything else is only meaningful if this is your machine.

tasks.title: Bluetooth adapter and radio state
tasks.reason: Layer D. Whether Windows even has a Bluetooth adapter, and whether it is present and enabled. A disabled radio explains a scan that finds nothing.
commands: Get-PnpDevice -Class Bluetooth | Where-Object { $_.FriendlyName -match 'Adapter|Radio' } | Select-Object Status,FriendlyName,InstanceId | Format-List

tasks.title: Bluetooth support service
tasks.reason: Layer C. The Windows Bluetooth stack is a service. If bthserv is stopped, every scan fails regardless of the adapter.

tasks.title: Paired and enumerated Bluetooth devices
tasks.reason: Layer F. What Windows believes is paired. The CMF Watch Pro 2 should appear here if it was ever paired.

tasks.title: Python and the BLE stack on the laptop
tasks.reason: Layer G/H. The previous workflow imported bleak. This establishes whether the same tooling is present, and where Python lives.

tasks.title: Controlled BLE scan (read-only, no connection)
tasks.reason: The decisive probe. A passive discovery scan. Advertises nothing, writes nothing, connects to nothing.

tasks.title: Does the watch specifically appear
tasks.reason: Same scan, filtered. The single line that answers whether the CMF Watch Pro 2 is visible over BLE right now.
commands: python -c "import asyncio,bleak;d=asyncio.run(bleak.BleakScanner.discover(timeout=10,return_adv=True));hits=[(a,v[1].local_name,v[0].name,v[1].rssi) for a,v in d.items() if any(s in ((v[1].local_name or '')+(v[0].name or '')).lower() for s in ('cmf','watch','nothing'))];print('MATCHES:',len(hits));[print(h) for h in hits]"

tasks.title: Prior CMF tooling already on this machine
tasks.reason: The previous workflow worked. Its scripts may still be on disk. Finding them avoids reinventing anything.
commands: Get-ChildItem -Path $env:USERPROFILE -Recurse -Depth 4 -Filter '*.py' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-String -Pattern 'BleakScanner|pair_and_probe|GETSECRET' -List -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -First 20 Path

Get-ChildItem -Path $env:USERPROFILE\Downloads,$env:USERPROFILE\Desktop,$env:USERPROFILE\Documents -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object Name,LastWriteTime | Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending | Select-Object -First 25

tasks.title: Network and session context
tasks.reason: What this PowerShell session can reach, and what long-running processes it has.

tasks.title: Separate check: adb location
tasks.reason: Unrelated to Bluetooth, kept separate on purpose. It resolves the empty A35 files: adb was not on PATH, so the phone batch ran no commands and posted empty headers.

after_this_batch: Report which layer works and which fails, with raw output as evidence.
If the watch appears in tasks 6/7, service and characteristic enumeration comes next, still read-only.
No writes to the watch until a read-only baseline is recorded and that specific write is approved.
